subject: Hosted API latency commitments — burst traffic evidence & rollforward proposal
messages:
From: Sarah Liang <sarah.liang@acmecorp.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify p50/p95 windowing for Hosted API — evidence for burst carveout

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the quick demo earlier. Procurement has one final ask before we can sign: we need clarity on how Redwood measures p50/p95 for the Hosted API during high-burst events and what evidence you will accept for a temporary window carveout. Specifically: 

- Are p50 and p95 calculated on per-request latency or per-token?
- Do you use rolling windows (e.g., 5m sliding) or fixed epoch windows (1h)?
- What constitutes an acceptable "burst" for which a transient carveout would be applied?

We'd like an amendment in the SOW that captures: measurement method, an agreed carveout definition, the evidence package you will provide, and the rollforward timeline if a carveout is approved.

Can you send your proposed language and sample evidence (logs/aggregates) by EOD Monday?

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Liang
Head of Cloud Procurement
Acme Corp

Attachment: acme_burst_analysis_q2.xlsx (stub)

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Sarah Liang <sarah.liang@acmecorp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify p50/p95 windowing for Hosted API — evidence for burst carveout

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear asks. See proposed SOW amendment text below and a short summary of the evidence bundle we'll provide. Happy to iterate.

Proposed SOW amendment (draft):
1) Measurement: Redwood will compute latency commitments on per-request end-to-end latency (request-receive to final byte of response). p50 and p95 are ticketed as request-level quantiles across the measurement window. Token-level metrics will be provided as supplementary telemetry but are not the contractual metric.

2) Windowing: Measurement windows will be fixed 60-minute epochs aligned to UTC (00:00-00:59, 01:00-01:59, ...). For operational clarity, Redwood will also publish 5-minute rolling percentile snapshots internally, but only 60-minute epochs are binding for SLA calculations.

3) Burst carveout definition: A burst event is defined as a contiguous 15-minute period where inbound request rate exceeds 5x the 95th percentile of Acme's historical hourly traffic baseline, and where the cluster-level queueing delay exceeds 50ms median across the affected shard set. RFC evidence required for carveout request: request-rate histogram, cluster CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth traces, and KV-cache hit-rate for the period in question.

4) Rollforward process: If Redwood approves a temporary carveout, the carveout will be time-limited to the affected 60-minute epochs and marked in the SLA report. Redwood will provide a remediation plan within 48 hours and a targeted rollforward (reinstatement of standard measurement) within 14 calendar days, or earlier with agreed mitigations.

Evidence package we will provide with any carveout approval request: aggregated request-level CSV, per-shard latency percentiles, telemetry snapshot (5min buckets), and a short incident write-up. We'll deliver a ZIP with logs and aggregates; sample file names are attached.

I've attached a sample "evidence bundle" spreadsheet and a template incident report to show how we'll present the data.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: requested_slo_evidence_bundle.zip (stub); slo-rollforward-template.docx (internal link)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify p50/p95 windowing for Hosted API — evidence for burst carveout

Mateo — suggested edits below (short):
- Change epoch window to UTC-aligned 1h, ok. Add explicit language: "Rolling 5-minute snapshots are provided for operational visibility and are not binding."
- For carveout definition, remove absolute "50ms" threshold and replace with "statistically significant queueing deviation (>=2 sigma above baseline)" to avoid hard numbers that vary by model class.
- Add a clause: "Redwood will not apply a retrospective carveout for events where the customer has enabled burst protection features (reserved capacity, routing limits) and those features were configured per Redwood recommendations."

I'll add the edits to legal's template and loop Lauren for SOW approval.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product (SLOs)
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Liang <sarah.liang@acmecorp.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify p50/p95 windowing for Hosted API — evidence for burst carveout

Thanks Mateo / Karthik — this reads well and answers most of our questions. A couple of notes from procurement/legal after a quick review: 

- Acme accepts the UTC-aligned 60-minute epoch approach.
- For the carveout, we want the 2-sigma statistical language (Karthik's suggestion) but also want Redwood to include a short mechanical test in the evidence bundle that shows the impact on customer-facing latency (sample 1-minute bucket visualization).
- We also want a max carveout duration clause: any approved carveout cannot exceed 3 contiguous epochs (3 hours) without a mutual review and documented plan.

I'll need the final SOW amendment text and a sample evidence ZIP by EOD Tuesday so our legal team can sign off. We'll attach that to the PO.

Regards,
Sarah
Head of Cloud Procurement
Acme Corp

Sarah — thanks. Attached is the finalized amendment language (ready for insertion into the SOW) and a mock evidence ZIP containing the CSVs and a one-page visualization for a sample burst. Key changes per your asks: 

- Replaced the hard 50ms threshold with ">=2 sigma" queueing deviation language.
- Added the mechanical 1-minute bucket visualization requirement to the evidence bundle.
- Added a max carveout duration: 3 contiguous epochs unless extended by mutual written agreement.
- Added the non-retrospective clause if Acme had burst protections enabled per Redwood guidance.

Next steps: once you confirm the insertion point in the SOW, we'll generate the final ZIP using your production telemetry for the last quarter and attach it to the procurement packet. I'll also open a DocuSign envelope for the amendment after Lauren confirms legal language.

Thanks,
Mateo
